findings.name: abdominal examination
findings.result: Severe epigastric tenderness; no abdominal distension.

findings.name: abdominal ultrasound
findings.result: Normal abdominal parenchyma, a normal gallbladder, and no common bile duct dilation.

findings.name: multidetector CT of the abdomen (portal phase)
findings.result: Cystic lesions encircling the second portion of the duodenum with circumferential duodenal wall thickening, and a soft-tissue component in the pancreaticoduodenal groove abutting the pancreatic head; the pancreatic head and pancreatic duct appear normal. Signs of inflammatory change, including fat stranding and fluid, surround the groove area.

findings.name: contrast-enhanced MRI of the abdomen
findings.result: Intramural fluid-signal lesions within the thickened duodenal wall and sheet-like tissue in the groove with enhancement patterns similar to the pancreas.

findings.name: MR cholangiopancreatography
findings.result: Normal gallbladder; no dilation of the common bile duct or pancreatic duct.

aliases: cystic dystrophy of the duodenal wall
pancreatic hamartoma of the duodenal wall
gold.reasoning: 1. Groove pancreatic carcinoma was considered; it was deemed less likely because “both duodenal wall thickening and cystic changes are findings extremely uncommon in pancreatic adenocarcinoma.” 2. Adenocarcinoma of the groove was further excluded as it “is homogeneously hypoenhancing compared with the pancreas,” unlike the heterogeneous, pancreas-like enhancement observed here. 3. Duodenal duplication cyst was considered but ruled out based on the intramural location within a thickened duodenal wall: “differentiating the duodenal cysts from duplication cysts is crucial to assess their location in the duodenal wall, which is also thickened.”
